scenes.visual: Slate. A chalk traffic light draws in, tilted slightly, like a sticker on a window. On 'red light' the top lamp fills chalk (no red). On 'listen to your engine' three small chalk sound arcs pulse beside it. Through the 1 s beat after the first line: only the lamp, breathing (tiny scale pulse), then the hum arcs.
changes: sound arcs on 'listen to your engine'
scenes.words: next time you're stopped at a red light listen to your engine

scenes.visual: The traffic light slides to the side; at centre an end-on chalk crank wheel turns steadily. A counter '700' with 'per minute' ticks up on 'seven hundred times a minute'.
changes: counter on 'seven hundred times a minute'
scenes.words: it's still turning around seven hundred times a minute

scenes.visual: The wheel stays; a one-second bar fills beside it with twelve chalk ticks, one per turn, flashing as the wheel passes. Label '≈ 12 turns every second'. A faint note: 'idle differs by engine'.
changes: 'idle differs by engine' on 'idles a little differently'
twelve ticks flash on 'twelve turns every second'
scenes.words: every engine idles a little differently but that's nearly twelve turns every second

scenes.visual: Four chalk slots in a row, each a mini piston stroke (down, up, down, up) with the labels in, squeeze, push, out. On 'only one stroke in every four actually pushes' slot three lights chalk bright and the other three go muted.
scenes.words: and in each cylinder only one stroke in every four actually pushes

scenes.visual: The three muted slots get a dashed muted momentum trail from a small flywheel at the right end, so they look pulled along. A single chalk word 'carried' under them.
changes: trail dashes in on 'isn't driving itself'
scenes.words: for the other three the engine isn't driving itself it's being carried

scenes.anchor: so today we're going to follow
scenes.visual: One cylinder outline appears at centre alone. A stopwatch ring shows a sixth of a circle filled in chalk, label '1/6 second'. On 'slowed right down' a muted fast ghost of the ring is replaced by the slow single hand.
changes: ring fills a sixth on 'about a sixth of a second'
scenes.words: so today we're going to follow one cycle of one cylinder about a sixth of a second of real time slowed right down

scenes.anchor: the clock in the corner is real time
scenes.visual: The clock and the crank-angle dial draw in at the top right (the only entrance of either): '0.000 s', dial at 0°, tag '0° = START OF INTAKE'. On 'how little of it is spent working' the three muted arcs light and the chalk arc is the only thick one. Then the frame eases to clean slate for the soft landing into the intro sting (music eases out).
changes: clock and dial enter on 'in the corner'
dial arcs split on 'how little of it'
frame eases to slate on 'spent working'
scenes.words: the clock in the corner is real time watch how little of it is spent working

scenes.visual: The cylinder cutaway (frozen H1 still: chalk on panel, no colour) draws in at centre, large, with the clock and dial live in the corner. Locator inset reads 'ENGINE'.
scenes.note: first appearance of the H1 cutaway; every later 2D aside sits on this frozen still
scenes.words: here's our cylinder

scenes.visual: Part isolation (look vocabulary 6), one subject at a time over the frozen cutaway: piston, then rod, then crankshaft each brighten in turn with the others dimmed; labels outside the shape. On 'heavy wheel' the flywheel brightens, rim ticks readable; on 'keep an eye on it' a soft ring pulses around it.
changes: flywheel on 'a heavy wheel called the flywheel'
ring pulses on 'keep an eye on it'
scenes.words: a piston a connecting rod a crankshaft and on the end of the crank a heavy wheel called the flywheel keep an eye on it

scenes.visual: Over the still: the two valves brighten; labels 'intake: air and fuel in' and 'exhaust: burnt gas out' outside the shape. On 'between them' the spark plug brightens, only its electrode tip lime-dotted, label 'spark plug'.
scenes.words: up top two valves one lets air and fuel in the other lets burnt gas out between them sits the spark plug

scenes.anchor: one full cycle takes two turns
scenes.visual: A chalk crank wheel turns twice; two full-circle outlines stack into '720°'. The dial at the corner is not touched.
changes: first turn on 'two turns of the crankshaft'
scenes.words: one full cycle takes two turns of the crankshaft seven hundred and twenty degrees

scenes.anchor: four strokes half a turn each
scenes.visual: The 720° ring splits into four 180° arcs labelled intake, compression, power, exhaust; the intake arc is chalk, the others muted (same grammar as the corner dial).
scenes.words: four strokes half a turn each

scenes.visual: A magnifier sweeps onto the corner dial and isolates a single degree tick; label '1° = 0.24 ms' (a quarter of a thousandth of a second). The hand moves one tick and the clock digits barely change.
changes: label on 'a quarter of a thousandth of a second'
scenes.words: at this speed each degree of that turn lasts about a quarter of a thousandth of a second

scenes.visual: HERO H1 cutaway, clip `intake` (5 s, constant crank speed, locked camera, 8 percent push): piston falls, intake valve open. Overlay: chapter tag 'STROKE 1 · INTAKE', 34 px mono 'OPEN' beside the intake valve, 'CLOSED' on the exhaust valve; dial arc 0-180 chalk, the rest muted. The flywheel rim ticks show the turn.
changes: piston ghost trail on 'the piston falls'
scenes.words: stroke one intake the intake valve is open and the piston falls

scenes.visual: Charge fill (vocab 2) over the frozen cutaway: a chalk 'suck' label with a muted cross-out on 'doesn't really suck'. A small gauge inside shows 'lower pressure'; outside 'higher pressure'. Violet charge dots stream through the intake valve on 'pushes the charge in' (no arrows: motion and dots only).
changes: 'suck' crossed out on 'doesn't really suck anything in'
'lower pressure inside' on 'lowers the pressure inside'
violet dots stream on 'pushes the charge in'
scenes.words: here's the first surprise the piston doesn't really suck anything in as it falls it lowers the pressure inside the cylinder and the air outside at higher pressure pushes the charge in through the open valve

scenes.anchor: but at idle there's a catch
scenes.visual: The intake pipe draws in beside the valve; a small tag 'AT IDLE'. The viewer sees a plain open pipe first, so the next scene's restriction reads as the catch.
scenes.words: but at idle there's a catch

scenes.anchor: the throttle the valve your accelerator
scenes.visual: A throttle plate in the pipe, partly closed (a chalk flap at 70 degrees); a dashed chalk link to a pedal icon labelled 'accelerator'. On 'pull its air in against a restriction' the violet dots squeeze through the gap and thin out behind it.
changes: pedal link on 'your accelerator pedal opens'
scenes.words: the throttle the valve your accelerator pedal opens is partly closed so the engine has to pull its air in against a restriction

scenes.visual: Title card 'THROTTLING' over the pipe; a bar labelled 'light load' sits low on an efficiency scale ('less efficient at light load'). On 'pumping losses' a small muted pump loop icon appears with the term.
scenes.words: that's called throttling and it's one main reason a gasoline engine is less efficient when it's only lightly loaded it adds to what engineers call pumping losses

scenes.anchor: and notice what's turning the crank
scenes.visual: Over the frozen cutaway: a small fuel drop icon crossed out on 'not fuel'; the flywheel brightens with a muted momentum trail (dashes, no arrowheads) tracing its rim. On 'pulling the piston down' the rod and piston brighten along the trail.
changes: piston brightens on 'pulling the piston down'
scenes.words: and notice what's turning the crank right now not fuel the flywheel its momentum is pulling the piston down

scenes.visual: The two valves brighten. A square-wave timing bar (dashed, idealised: opens exactly at the end) appears as 'what you'd guess', then a rounded real lift curve overdraws it on 'don't snap open and shut'.
changes: dashed ideal bar on 'don't snap open'
real lift curve on 'exactly at the ends of the strokes'
scenes.words: watch the valves too they don't snap open and shut exactly at the ends of the strokes

scenes.anchor: the intake valve opened a little
scenes.visual: The 720° dial redrawn large: the intake window as an arc that starts slightly before the top mark (OPEN tag) and ends well after the bottom mark (CLOSED tag). Piston icons at top and bottom mark the two moments.
changes: arc opens early on 'opened a little before'
scenes.words: the intake valve opened a little before the piston reached the top and it will close well after the piston has passed the bottom

scenes.visual: A chalk lobed cam disc turns at half the crank wheel's speed beside the crank wheel; label 'HALF SPEED' once. On 'only opens once every two turns' the valve lifts once while the crank wheel completes two turns.
changes: 'HALF SPEED' on 'half the speed of the crank'
valve lifts once on 'once every two turns'
scenes.words: they're worked by a camshaft which turns at half the speed of the crank because each valve only opens once every two turns

scenes.anchor: clock four hundredths of a second
scenes.visual: The corner clock grows to the centre and reads '0.043 s'; the intake arc closes. Under it a counter 'work made so far: 0' stays at zero. Then it shrinks back to the corner.
changes: '0' counter on 'nothing has been made yet'
scenes.words: clock four hundredths of a second one stroke done and nothing has been made yet

scenes.visual: HERO H1 cutaway, clip `compression` (5 s): both valves closed, the piston climbs, violet dots keep their count while the volume shrinks, so density rises (no colour change). Overlay: chapter tag 'STROKE 2 · COMPRESSION', 'CLOSED' tags on both valves, dial arc 180-360 chalk.
changes: label 'small space at the top' on 'small space at the top'
scenes.words: stroke two compression the intake valve closes and the piston climbs squeezing the mixture into the small space at the top

scenes.visual: Two cylinder sections side by side with identical violet dot counts: left at the bottom (big volume), right at the top (small volume). Labels 'volume at the bottom' and 'volume left at the top'; a divider bar reads 'compression ratio'.
changes: left section on 'volume at the bottom'
right section on 'space that's left at the top'
scenes.words: how hard it squeezes is called the compression ratio the volume at the bottom divided by the space that's left at the top

scenes.anchor: in a typical gasoline car engine
scenes.visual: A ratio counter rolls '10 : 1' and then '12 : 1', with a bracket 'typical gasoline car'.
scenes.words: in a typical gasoline car engine that's roughly ten to one up to about twelve to one

scenes.visual: A bar 'efficiency' rises as the ratio dial turns up.
scenes.words: squeeze harder and you get better efficiency

scenes.visual: The ratio counter keeps climbing past 12 : 1 and hits a chalk wall labelled '?'. Single tag 'WHY STOP?'.
scenes.words: so why stop there

scenes.anchor: because squeezing the mixture makes it hotter
scenes.visual: A chalk thermometer beside the compressed section fills with a heat-soft level that rises as the piston climbs. The compressed dots get a thin heat-soft edge.
scenes.words: because squeezing the mixture makes it hotter

scenes.visual: The thermometer passes a dashed limit line. In the chamber a pocket of unburned mixture, far from where the flame would be, flashes orange by itself. Tag 'KNOCK' appears on 'that's knock'.
scenes.words: push it past a limit and the unburned mixture can ignite by itself that's knock

scenes.anchor: the sudden release sends pressure waves
scenes.visual: Concentric dashed pressure ripples cross the chamber (no arrowheads). A chalk sound-wave glyph for 'the knocking sound'. On 'damage the engine' a muted crack runs across the piston crown.
changes: ripples on 'pressure waves through the cylinder'
scenes.words: the sudden release sends pressure waves through the cylinder that's the knocking sound and in severe cases it can damage the engine

scenes.anchor: a few engines push the limit
scenes.visual: The ratio counter rolls to '14 : 1' with a chalk car-badge card 'Mazda Skyactiv-G'.
scenes.words: a few engines push the limit mazda's skyactiv g reached fourteen to one

scenes.anchor: and this is where the number
scenes.visual: A chalk fuel-pump nozzle with a label plate '87'. The plate zooms toward the viewer.
scenes.words: and this is where the number on the fuel pump comes in

scenes.anchor: octane isn't a measure of how much
scenes.visual: A muted energy-bolt icon beside 'octane' is struck through. Label 'NOT ENERGY'.
scenes.words: octane isn't a measure of how much energy is in the fuel

scenes.anchor: it measures how well the fuel resists
scenes.visual: A resistance meter 'knock resistance' fills; the pump plate '87' sits at a point on it.
changes: meter fills on 'resists igniting by itself'
scenes.words: it measures how well the fuel resists igniting by itself under compression

scenes.anchor: it's tested in a special engine
scenes.visual: A chalk test-engine box with its own ratio dial turning up on 'raises its compression'; a knock tag flashes on 'until the fuel knocks'. Two reference columns draw on 'two reference fuels': 'iso-octane 100' and 'heptane 0' with the sample's reading placed between them.
changes: ratio dial turns on 'raises its compression'
knock tag on 'until the fuel knocks'
scenes.words: it's tested in a special engine that raises its compression until the fuel knocks and compared against two reference fuels iso octane rated one hundred and heptane rated zero

scenes.anchor: in the united states regular is generally
scenes.visual: Three chalk pump buttons: 'regular 87', 'premium 91 to 94'.
scenes.words: in the united states regular is generally eighty seven and premium ninety one to ninety four

scenes.visual: A balance: compression ratio on one pan, knock resistance on the other, rising together. Tag 'TRADE-OFF'.
changes: balance on 'needs fuel that resists knock'
scenes.words: higher compression needs fuel that resists knock that's the trade off

scenes.anchor: and this stroke too is paid for
scenes.visual: Back on the frozen cutaway: the flywheel with its muted momentum trail pulls the piston up; 'paid for by the flywheel'.
changes: trail on 'paid for by the flywheel'
scenes.words: and this stroke too is paid for by the flywheel

scenes.visual: Clock grows centre: '0.086 s', the compression arc closes. The dial shows half a revolution complete. Counter 'work made so far: 0' still zero.
scenes.words: clock nine hundredths of a second half the cycle gone still no work done

scenes.anchor: now something happens before the piston
scenes.visual: Tag 'ZOOM · LAST 30° OF COMPRESSION' (the dial hand stays at 360° / 0.086 s: this is a close look, not later in time). A one-cycle pressure trace (vocab 5) draws: chalk line rising, with a dotted TOP marker. The corner clock does not move.
changes: pressure trace draws on 'before the piston reaches the top'
scenes.note: decision for the showrunner: the approved script says the clock reads 0.086 s before the spark, so this chapter is a replay, not a continuation
scenes.words: now something happens before the piston reaches the top

scenes.visual: H1 moment: the cutaway is nearly colourless; the lime arc fires at the electrode (6 frame glow), a few tens of degrees before the top mark on the trace. SPARK marker on the trace, dial untouched.
text: a few tens of degrees early
scenes.words: the spark fires a few tens of degrees early

scenes.anchor: why early because burning takes time
scenes.visual: A chalk stopwatch with a ring that fills while the piston icon keeps rising: label 'burning takes time'.
changes: ring fills on 'because burning takes time'
scenes.words: why early because burning takes time

scenes.anchor: the spark doesn't set off an explosion
scenes.visual: A chalk 'BANG' burst appears and is crossed out in muted; the word 'explosion' under it.
scenes.words: the spark doesn't set off an explosion

scenes.anchor: it starts a tiny hot kernel
scenes.visual: HERO H2 flame front (6 s clip, close on the chamber, emission only): lime flash, a small orange kernel, a wrinkled orange front spreading through violet charge; behind the front the charge turns heat-soft, ahead it stays violet. Overlay labels: 'kernel', 'flame front', 'wrinkled by swirling air'.
changes: 'burned' fills on 'until it has all burned'
scenes.words: it starts a tiny hot kernel which grows into a flame wrinkled by the swirling air it sweeps outward through the mixture until it has all burned

scenes.visual: A burn-progress plot: x crank degrees, y fraction burned, an S-curve; a marker at 50 percent reads '≈ 25° of crank rotation'. Source tag 'MIT figures, modern engine'.
changes: plot draws on 'figures for a modern engine'
50 percent marker on 'half the mixture has burned'
scenes.words: in mit's figures for a modern engine half the mixture has burned only after about twenty five degrees of crank rotation

scenes.visual: Pressure trace again: the peak lands just after the top mark with the piston icon able to use it. Tag 'PEAK just after the top'.
changes: peak on 'pressure peak just after the top'
piston icon on 'where the piston can use it'
scenes.words: so the spark is timed to put the pressure peak just after the top where the piston can use it

scenes.visual: Trace variant: spark moved later, peak low and late; heat-soft area under the trace arrives after the piston is already low. Tag 'too late: heat can't be used'.
changes: spark moves later on 'fire too late'
heat-soft area on 'too far into the stroke'
scenes.words: fire too late and the heat arrives too far into the stroke to be turned into work

scenes.visual: Trace variant: spark moved earlier, peak before the top, a heat-soft puff leaking from the chamber. Tags 'wasted heat' and 'knock more likely'.
changes: spark moves earlier on 'fire too early'
scenes.words: fire too early and the engine wastes heat and makes knock more likely

scenes.anchor: because the abnormal much faster burn
scenes.visual: Knock vs smooth burn (vocab 9): two chamber sections side by side. Left: a clean spreading front. Right: a second orange pocket ignites ahead of the front by itself. Labels 'smooth burn' and 'knock'.
changes: both sections on 'much faster burn is knock'
scenes.words: because the abnormal much faster burn is knock the mixture ahead of the flame igniting by itself

scenes.visual: A chalk knock sensor icon on the block with sound arcs; the SPARK marker on the trace slides later. Two tags: 'less power', 'worse economy'.
changes: marker slides later on 'delay the spark'
scenes.words: modern engines listen for it and delay the spark to stop it at some cost in power and fuel economy

scenes.visual: HERO H1 cutaway, clip `power` (5 s): both valves closed, the burnt gas (heat-soft) pushes the piston down hard; dial arc 360-540 chalk. Overlay: chapter tag 'STROKE 3 · POWER', a pressure bar over the piston rising on 'raises the pressure', the flywheel gets its muted momentum trail on 'pushes the piston down'.
changes: piston push on 'pushes the piston down'
scenes.words: stroke three power the burning gas raises the pressure and pushes the piston down

scenes.visual: Over the frozen cutaway: the power arc glows chalk and a counter 'work made: +' flips on. Words 'ONLY HERE'.
changes: arc glows on 'this and only this'
counter flips on 'the engine does its work'
scenes.words: this and only this is where the engine does its work

scenes.anchor: half a turn about four hundredths
scenes.visual: The dial arc (180° wide) pulses; the clock label compares '0.043 s' next to the arc.
changes: '0.043 s' on 'four hundredths of a second'
scenes.words: half a turn about four hundredths of a second

scenes.visual: The flywheel's muted momentum trail grows (stored push) and then spreads along the next three dial arcs (muted) as it is given back. 'smoother pulses' bar flattens from a spike on 'evens out the pulses'.
changes: trail grows on 'stores some of that push'
trail spreads on 'over the next three strokes'
spike flattens on 'evens out the pulses'
scenes.words: and the flywheel stores some of that push and gives it back over the next three strokes that evens out the pulses

scenes.anchor: a single cylinder fires only once
scenes.visual: A 720° timeline with one chalk bump (the power stroke) and a long muted flat; label 'once every two turns'.
scenes.words: a single cylinder fires only once every two turns

scenes.visual: Four small cylinders line up under the timeline, each with its own chalk bump staggered.
changes: cylinders appear on 'engines share the job'
scenes.words: so engines share the job

scenes.visual: The staggered bumps with a ruler: '180°' between each. Four-cylinder card 'every 180°'.
scenes.words: in a four cylinder engine a power stroke starts every hundred and eighty degrees

scenes.visual: HERO H3 four-cylinder crank (7 s, crank and pistons only): one throw chalk-bright and pushing, three muted; the lit throw rotates 1-3-4-2 every 180°. Overlay: 'FIRING ORDER 1-3-4-2', labels on the muted throws 'in', 'squeeze', 'out'.
changes: 'each cylinder on a different stroke' on 'a different stroke'
labels on 'breathe in squeeze and breathe out'
scenes.words: a common firing order is one three four two so at any moment each cylinder is on a different stroke one pushing while the others breathe in squeeze and breathe out

scenes.anchor: six cylinders a power stroke every
scenes.visual: Two more timeline strips: six cylinders '120°', eight cylinders '90°'.
scenes.words: six cylinders a power stroke every hundred and twenty degrees eight every ninety

scenes.visual: The power bumps of the strips overlap: summed curve flattens: 'smoother'.
changes: curve flattens on 'the smoother the engine runs'
scenes.words: the more cylinders the more those pushes overlap and the smoother the engine runs

scenes.visual: Clock grows centre: '0.129 s'. Three of four arcs complete, power arc chalk. Then the dial prepares to freeze (dims on the next line).
scenes.words: clock thirteen hundredths of a second

scenes.visual: The clock and dial freeze at 0.129 s and dim to muted; 34 px tag 'CLOCK STOPPED'. The cylinder fades out; the slate is empty for a beat.
scenes.words: let's stop the clock for a moment

scenes.anchor: this four-stroke cycle is often called
scenes.visual: Title card 'THE OTTO CYCLE'; below it a small question 'whose cycle?'.
scenes.words: this four stroke cycle is often called the otto cycle

scenes.visual: Name card with the public-domain Otto portrait (asset I1, c. 1868, Commons) in a chalk frame: 'Nikolaus Otto · German gas-engine builder'. Credit line 'portrait: unknown, c. 1868 (public domain)'.
scenes.words: nikolaus otto was a german gas engine builder

scenes.visual: Second name card beside Otto's: 'Eugen Langen · Otto's partner' (no portrait; name card only). A chalk medal icon '1867 Paris exhibition · gold medal · earlier gas engine'.
changes: Langen card on 'his partner eugen langen'
'earlier gas engine' on 'for an earlier gas engine'
scenes.words: with his partner eugen langen he'd already won a gold medal at the eighteen sixty seven paris exhibition for an earlier gas engine

scenes.visual: A chalk timeline: '1867' (earlier gas engine) then '1876' with a four-stroke engine box; a sales-curve tick 'immediate commercial success'.
scenes.words: in eighteen seventy six otto built an engine on the four stroke principle it was an immediate commercial success

scenes.visual: Patent sheet US 194,047 (asset P1, 14 Aug 1877, USPTO, public domain) in a chalk frame with a slow pan over the flywheel and cylinder. Caption 'Otto, US patent 1877: a gas engine with a layered charge' (not the modern engine).
changes: highlight on 'flywheel's momentum driving the piston back'
pan to the cylinder on 'four strokes'
scenes.words: his american patent from eighteen seventy seven describes the same four strokes with the flywheel's momentum driving the piston back

scenes.visual: The Otto name card slides left; an empty chalk frame with a dashed outline appears to its right with a question 'first?'.
scenes.words: but otto wasn't the first to describe it

scenes.anchor: in eighteen sixty-two a french engineer
scenes.visual: Name card, no portrait: 'ALPHONSE BEAU DE ROCHAS', 'French engineer', '1862: set out the cycle on paper'. A sheet icon gets four stroke sketches; on 'never built an engine' a dashed empty engine outline appears beside it.
changes: dashed engine on 'never built an engine'
text: 1862: set out the cycle on paper
scenes.words: in eighteen sixty two a french engineer alphonse beau de rochas had set out the four stroke cycle on paper he never built an engine

scenes.anchor: in eighteen eighty-six after that earlier
scenes.visual: A chalk patent document 'Otto, German patent' gets a muted diagonal stamp 'REVOKED 1886' next to the 1862 sheet marked 'brought to light'.
scenes.words: in eighteen eighty six after that earlier description was brought to light otto's german patent was revoked

scenes.anchor: his patent was really about a layered charge
scenes.visual: A chamber section with violet charge in layers (dense near the plug, thinner away). Quote card in chalk: 'instead of an explosion ensuing, the flame passes gradually from one particle to another'.
changes: quote on 'instead of an explosion ensuing'
particles hop layer to layer on 'one particle to another'
scenes.words: his patent was really about a layered charge of fuel it says that instead of an explosion ensuing the flame passes gradually from one particle to another

scenes.visual: The layers dissolve to a uniform violet charge; an orange wrinkled front still sweeps across. Tag 'a spreading flame, not a bang'.
changes: layers dissolve on 'don't use his layered charge'
text: a spreading flame, not a bang
scenes.words: today's engines don't use his layered charge but the burn is still a spreading flame not a bang

scenes.visual: The frozen clock re-brightens to full chalk, the 'CLOCK STOPPED' tag clears and the cylinder cutaway returns.
changes: clock resumes on 'back to the clock'
scenes.words: back to the clock

scenes.visual: HERO H1 cutaway, clip `exhaust` (5 s): the exhaust valve open, the piston rises, burnt gas (heat-soft) leaves as orange-edged particles. changes: 'OPEN' on 'valve opened just before the bottom'
bar drops on 'let the pressure drop'

scenes.words: stroke four exhaust the exhaust valve opened just before the bottom of the power stroke to let the pressure drop it costs a little work but it's a net gain

scenes.visual: Over the frozen cutaway: a small heat arrow (the only arrowhead) at the exhaust port as orange-edged particles leave; muted trail from the flywheel.
changes: particles leave on 'pushes the burnt gas out'
scenes.words: now the piston rises and pushes the burnt gas out

scenes.anchor: near the top for a short moment
scenes.visual: Both valves highlighted chalk emphasis for about 2 s, the rest dimmed; tag 'VALVE OVERLAP' on 'engineers call it'.
changes: both valves on 'both valves are open together'

changes: bracket on 'between twelve and thirty percent'
qualifier on 'depending on how it's driven'

scenes.visual: The dial ring fills once completely, caption 'ONE CYCLE'.

changes: two turns on 'two turns of the crank'
chalk arc on 'only one of them pushing'

scenes.anchor: three strokes out of every four
scenes.visual: Three muted strokes with a dashed momentum trail to the flywheel and to neighbouring cylinder icons: 'carried by the flywheel and the others'.
changes: trail to flywheel on 'a heavy spinning wheel'
trails to neighbours on 'the cylinders next to it'
